newsitem.title: ZAIRE: South Africa's Mbeki arrives for talks with Kabila.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mbeki arrives for talks with Kabila.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki arrived in the southeastern Zairean city of Lubumbashi on Sunday for talks with Laurent Kabila, whose alliance has proclaimed victory in the civil war.
Mbeki told reporters at Lubumbashi airport that it seemed clear to South Africa that the process of transition agreed upon by Kabila and ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko was on course.

"It's on course...it seems clear to us that the country is in the course of that process that was agreed by everybody -- setting up a transitional authority that will take charge of affairs," Mbeki added.
The South African news agency SAPA said Mbeki was accompanied by Defence Minister Joe Modise, Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Aziz Pahad and director-general Frank Chikane.
Talks were planned for Sunday night in Lubumbashi, it said.
Pilots who flew Mbeki's delegation in said it appeared to them that they would stay overnight in the Kabila headquarters.

South Africa Foreign Affairs Minister Alfred Nzo said there was "no reason" why Pretoria would not support Kabila. "The people of Zaire will decide, but there is no reason why we would not support him," SAPA quoted Nzo as saying.

Earlier, Kabila and his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo met United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun and pledged to fully cooperate with U.N. and other humanitarian agencies dealing with the refugee crisis.

Sahnoun, accompanied by a special representative of the OAU (Organisation of African Unity), Mamadou Kamme, met Kabila as a delegation of Alliance leaders prepared to leave for Kinshasa to reassure the capital city's population about security.
He left Kinshasa after the talks for the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa to brief the OAU and then to New York where he would brief the Security Council on the situation in Zaire.
